messages:
angela: @sai FYI — customer (ACME Corp) on private VPC asked whether we can 'pass through' our reserved/commitment discounts to their invoice and fold the GPU license into a single monthly line. They want predictable billing. What are options and legal/licensing implications?

mike: short answer: we don't directly assign cloud commitments to customers today. Commitments live in our account and savings get amortized. Options: (1) absorb savings and lower list price; (2) show a 'commitment allocation' credit on invoice (internal reconciliation needed); (3) offer a dedicated/reserved contract where customer pays for the reservation and we provide infra management. Metering note: private nodes report usage via meter-agent v2 so we can produce region-by-region usage exports. :thinking:

oli: from solutions: customers usually want simplicity. If ACME insists on seeing the saving, I'd recommend C — dedicated/reserved with explicit pass-through (they take the commitment). For transparency without transfer, we can produce a line showing "Estimated commitment allocation" but must label it clearly as an internal allocation, not a vendor-assigned discount.

sai: they want a single predictable invoice amount each month — not a usage bill with variable cloud pass-through. Can we offer a fixed monthly invoice that includes an explicit "commitment credit"?

mike: region constraint: commitments are regional (e.g., eu-west-2 vs us-west-2). We can't shift regional commitments easily. If customer's footprint spans regions we need to allocate savings pro-rata per region usage. Also reserved GPU SKUs differ by family — mapping must be explicit.

jen: legal check: do NOT imply we're reselling or transferring a third-party committed discount unless there's an explicit contractual assignment with the cloud vendor. Cloud contracts often prohibit representing vendor discounts as customer-held savings unless they sign/assume the commitment. We can provide an "allocation" as a commercial courtesy but add disclaimers.

billing-bot: Invoice preview (sample allocation approach):
```
Line 1: Cloud compute (gross) - eu-west-2: $9,400
Line 2: Cloud compute (gross) - us-west-2: $3,050
Line 3: Commitment allocation (eu-west-2) -$2,600
Line 4: Commitment allocation (us-west-2) -$450
Line 5: Redwood platform license (GPU runtime + support): $4,500
Line 6: Network egress: $210
Total due: $13,710
Note: 'Commitment allocation' is an internal allocation of our amortized savings; not a vendor-assigned transfer.
```

angela: ok — two asks: (A) infra to produce a reproducible export that shows per-region gross cloud charges + allocation fields so finance can surface it as separate invoice lines, (B) legal to draft clear language/disclaimer for customer MSA. Need a sample by EOD Friday to show ACME.

mike: i'll add a BigQuery export mapping in the meter-agent repo and a sample SQL that computes pro-rata allocation. PR target: Thu EOD. Will include a sample mapping table with reserved SKU family keys and region tags. :thumbsup:

oli: i'll draft a one-page invoice sample and a short customer note explaining options (fixed monthly vs allocation). will ping AE to present.

jen: i'll prepare two clause options: (1) allocation + disclaimer, (2) assignment/resale language if they want to assume commitments. will review with procurement.

angela: perfect. action items: mike (infra) mapping + PR, oli (solutions) invoice + note, jen (legal) clause options. i'll coordinate with @sai to run this past the customer once we have artifacts. Thanks everyone. :eyes:
